title: Python / Colab Bridge Packet v2

canonical_node.axiom: Every runtime result must have four things before it supports a public claim: exact artifact path, variable/unit/range declaration, side-by-side baseline or ablation control, and output hash or rerun receipt.
definitions: Runtime artifact: a notebook, script, or output file produced by Python/Colab execution.
Variable/parameter registry: a CSV listing symbols and parameters extracted from runtime artifacts.
Dimensional audit queue: a CSV tracking which symbols need units, ranges, normalization, and source notes.
Ablation/control matrix: a CSV ensuring every public-facing runtime claim runs beside a null, rival, or broken-control version.
Public claim: a statement presented as supported by runtime evidence.
derivation: The packet introduces a variable and parameter registry extracted from runtime artifacts.
It introduces a dimensional audit queue for deciding which symbols need units, ranges, normalization, and source notes.
It introduces an ablation/control matrix so every public-facing runtime claim runs beside a null, rival, or broken-control version.
The main rule states that every runtime result should have four things before it supports a public claim.
The packet identifies safe first public-support candidates and risky ones that should become objection/repair pages until rerun evidence settles them.
canonical_node.action: Before any runtime result is used to support a public claim, ensure it has: exact artifact path, variable/unit/range declaration, side-by-side baseline or ablation control, and output hash or rerun receipt. Use the provided registries and matrices as the first tools for this check.
boundary: This packet does not itself verify any runtime result.
It does not provide proof of correctness for any claim.
It does not resolve open/conflicted artifacts.
It does not replace the Lean proof ledger.
test: Check that each public-facing runtime claim has an associated artifact path.
Check that each symbol/parameter has a unit/range declaration or is in the dimensional audit queue.
Check that each claim has a side-by-side baseline or ablation control.
Check that each claim has an output hash or rerun receipt.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a structured bridge between Lean proof ledger and runtime notebooks/scripts by introducing registries, audit queues, and ablation matrices.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the requirement that runtime results must be traceable and reproducible before supporting public claims.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this packet, runtime results lack a standardized method for tracking variables, dimensions, and controls, making public claims unsupported.

classification.recommended_atom_action: adopt as procedural rule; do not treat as proof

overstatement_risks: Treating the packet as evidence of verification rather than as a checklist.
Assuming that having the four items guarantees correctness.
Using the packet to claim that runtime results are proven.
kill_conditions: If the registries or matrices are not maintained or are incomplete.
If the four required items are not actually enforced.
If the packet is used to claim verification without rerun evidence.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the four-item checklist as a guardrail in the Lean proof ledger.

plain_summary: This packet establishes a procedural rule: before any runtime result can support a public claim, it must have an artifact path, variable/unit/range declaration, baseline/ablation control, and output hash/rerun receipt. It introduces registries and matrices to track these, but does not itself verify any results.
